newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: India sees steady growth in Third World trade.
newsitem.headline: India sees steady growth in Third World trade.

text.p: A senior Indian trade official said on Tuesday trade among 16 Third World states called the Group of 15 (G-15) had grown considerably in the last two years.
A.N. Ram, permanent secretary for economic relations at India's foreign affairs ministry, told Reuters at the end of a three-day G-15 summit in Zimbabwe:
"The intra-G-15 trade is today in the region of $55 billion and I would say it has grown considerably as compared to last year and the year before". He gave no figures for 1994 and 1995.
Ram said one hindrance to trade among developing countries was lack of knowledge of what goods and services each country had on offer.

The G-15 retains its original name although it now comprises 16 countries -- Algeria, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Jamaica, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Senegal, Peru, Venezuela, Yugoslavia and Zimbabwe.
